name: sandbox-verify
summary: Run each task's acceptance test (feature.ps1 verify) and every phase test inside the sandbox, as designed in docs/designs/sandbox-verify.md (locked 2026-11-20). Phase 1 adds -SandboxRun -Worktree/-Feature, the tail field and the .venv exclude to the delegate skill. Phase 2 makes verify call it: first the host-side refactors and the -OnHost path (verify-host), then the sandboxed path (verify-sandbox), with the stage and skill docs (build-docs) in parallel. The design's single verify-sandbox task is split in two here because it touches feature.ps1 and feature.Tests.ps1 heavily; verify-host lands the parts that do not need delegate.ps1. Phase 1 and phase 2's task checks run under today's rules (on the host); the first sandboxed run is phase 2's phase test, which is the full suite and therefore includes the delegate tests that need the host: under D1 the lead expects to ask the user for one host run there. Lead steps at sign-off: the three lead-run checks in the design's Verification section, docs/test-plan.md and docs/HANDOFF.md. No steps for the user. Deviations from the locked design, which this plan supersedes: the phase tests follow the plan rules (phase 1 runs scripts/test.ps1 -Fast, phase 2 the full suite) instead of the design's Phases rows, so the design's sentence 'No host run is expected there' does not hold; at phase 2's end the full suite runs through -SandboxRun, the delegate tests fail there as measured, and the lead asks the user for one host run, logged with feature.ps1 decision -Kind decision -Text 'host run: phase 2, approved: <words>' before running the suite in <repo>. In the design's Mapping rule, an ok:false whose error starts with 'sandbox: no free slot' is slot-busy, checked before the generic ok:false -> sandbox-error rule (as the design's Data section defines slot-busy). Merge order: build-docs may merge before verify-sandbox; the lead follows the updated build.md only after verify-sandbox is merged, and the phase-2 phase test is the first step that uses it. build-docs is prose: its acceptance command checks that key strings are present, and the lead reads the text against the design.

phases.rationale: The delegate side first: verify depends on -SandboxRun -Worktree, -Feature and tail, whose contracts are fixed in the design's Data and Rules sections.

tasks.title: -SandboxRun -Worktree and -Feature, tail, .venv exclude
tasks.test: pwsh -NoProfile -c '$c = New-PesterConfiguration; $c.Run.Path = @("skills/delegate/tests/DelegateLaunch.Tests.ps1", "skills/delegate/tests/Sandbox.Tests.ps1"); $c.Filter.FullName = @("*SandboxRun*", "*command tail*", "*delegate parameter sets*", "*environment gate*"); $c.TestRegistry.Enabled = $false; $c.Run.Exit = $true; Invoke-Pester -Configuration $c'
tasks.brief: Implement the delegate side of docs/designs/sandbox-verify.md exactly as its Data and Rules sections state: in delegate.ps1, -Worktree and -Feature in the SandboxRun parameter set (refuse -Worktree with an explicitly bound -Base), the path normalization and the three -Worktree checks with their exact errors, one shared helper for the probe and -Worktree forms (only the probe form removes a worktree, and only a .probe- leaf), run name probe-<hex> for both forms, the pid file runs\probe-<hex>.pid holding {pid, startTime, feature} written before the helper and removed in an outer finally, tail in the JSON output for ran and timeout, and Add-DelegateVenvExclude (append .venv/ to the shared .git/info/exclude once, with a leading newline when the file does not end with one) called right before each Add-SandboxEnvLinks call (the helper and the worker launch). In Sandbox.psm1, Invoke-SandboxCommand also returns tail: a string array of the last 40 lines of stdout.txt then stderr.txt, each cut at 400 characters, from a new function Get-SandboxCommandTailLines beside Get-SandboxCommandOutputLines. Tests: a new Describe 'SandboxRun worktree' in DelegateLaunch.Tests.ps1 (refusals untagged; container cases tagged Sandbox and skipped like 'SandboxRun command') covering the cases in the design's Files row, and a new Describe 'Sandbox command tail' in Sandbox.Tests.ps1 with the three unit cases. Existing 'SandboxRun command', 'delegate parameter sets' and 'environment gate' tests must still pass; update the parameter-set test if it counts SandboxRun's parameters. The .venv exclude test's 'file does not end with a newline' case is reached by pre-seeding the test repo's .git/info/exclude with the text '.xagent/' and no line terminator before the run (delegate.ps1's startup check then finds .xagent/ and appends nothing, so Add-DelegateVenvExclude sees a file without a trailing newline).

phases.rationale: verify uses the new -SandboxRun. The host-side refactors come first so the sandboxed path and its tests build on them; the docs depend only on the interfaces fixed in the design.

tasks.title: verify refactors, -OnHost, where and setup in the schema
tasks.brief: In feature.ps1, per the design's Rules: move the wrapper text of Invoke-TaskTestCommand into New-TaskTestWrapper -TestCommand (returns the UTF-16LE base64) and have Invoke-TaskTestCommand call it, with unchanged behaviour; move the body of Invoke-DecisionFeature into Add-FeatureDecision -Repository -FeatureName -Kind -Text (returns the line, throws on failure; Invoke-DecisionFeature calls it and prints as today); add -OnHost to verify (the existing -Quote parameter is reused): -OnHost requires -Quote, -Quote requires -OnHost, and -OnHost logs 'host run: <task>, approved: <quote>' through Add-FeatureDecision before the test, refusing with {ok:false,error} and running nothing if that throws. In this task verify still runs every test on the host as today (the sandboxed default comes in verify-sandbox), so a run without -OnHost gives where: host and setup: null, and a run with -OnHost gives where: host. Add where (enum sandbox|host, required) and setup (required; null or {status enum environment-missing|slot-busy|sandbox-error, message, proposal}) to verify.schema.json and to the stored test object; update samples/verify.json, add samples/verify-setup.json and add it to $validSamples in the schemas Describe. Tests: -OnHost with and without -Quote, -Quote alone, the decision line, -OnHost refused with no test run when not on feature/<name>, and where/setup in output and state.json; existing verify tests keep passing unchanged except for asserting the new fields. Fixed details: (1) verify's order is -TimeoutSec check, -OnHost/-Quote pairing, worktree checks, then (sandboxed only, in verify-sandbox) the delegate.ps1 path and command length, then the host-run decision line, then the scope check, then the test; when any earlier refusal fires, no host-run line is written (assert this in the refusal tests). (2) verify calls Assert-OneLine 'Quote' $Quote, and an empty -Quote counts as missing ('-OnHost requires -Quote with the user's approval'), as gate does. (3) Schema: setup is null or an object with required status (enum environment-missing, slot-busy, sandbox-error), message (string) and proposal (object or null), no other properties; where is required with enum sandbox, host. (4) Samples: samples/verify.json gets "where": "sandbox" and "setup": null (the final contract; the schema allows both values); add verify-setup.json (environment-missing, a message, a proposal object, passed false, exitCode -1, tail "") and verify-error.json (sandbox-error, a message, proposal null, passed false, exitCode -1, tail ""), and add both to $validSamples. (5) This task's default host run gives where: host on purpose; verify-sandbox changes the default to where: sandbox.

tasks.title: verify runs the test through -SandboxRun -Worktree
tasks.brief: Make the sandboxed run verify's default, exactly as the design's Data and Rules sections state: refusal order (-TimeoutSec with the 30-3600 range for sandboxed runs, -OnHost/-Quote, worktree, delegate.ps1 path from <skill dir>/../delegate or XAGENT_DELEGATE_SCRIPT, the 30,000-character command-line limit, then the host-run decision); the -Command text with the [Console]::OutputEncoding statement, the inner pwsh -EncodedCommand from New-TaskTestWrapper and a literal exit $LASTEXITCODE, built from single-quoted strings; ProcessStartInfo with ArgumentList and asynchronous ReadToEndAsync reads; the <timeout> + <grace> wait (XAGENT_VERIFY_GRACE_SEC) with process-tree kill; JSON from the last non-empty stdout line; and the mapping to test {passed, exitCode, tail, where: sandbox, setup}, including slot-busy, the timeout line, and tail joined from -SandboxRun's tail array. Write fake-delegate.ps1 with the modes and exact JSON in the design's Files row, recording its arguments to fake-delegate-args.txt beside -Worktree. In feature.Tests.ps1, set XAGENT_DELEGATE_SCRIPT to the fake in the 'feature.ps1 verify' Describe and handle every existing and new test as the design's feature.Tests.ps1 row lists, all tagged Slow; add Describe 'live sandbox verify' tagged Live as the design's Verification section describes (own Describe, real delegate.ps1, self-contained skip, local $TestDrive on the repo's drive, a file at an absolute path in the real TestDrive). Do not run the Live test: the sandbox the worker runs in cannot create sandboxes. Fixed details: (1) Tests written by verify-host: the tests of a default run (without -OnHost) that assert where: host are changed to assert where: sandbox (they now go through the fake), including the state.json assertion; the -OnHost tests (with and without -Quote, -Quote alone, the decision line, the off-branch refusal) stay -OnHost and unchanged. (2) Before Start(), set StandardOutputEncoding and StandardErrorEncoding to [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false); the non-ASCII test reads through that path. (3) The command-line limit: refuse when the sum of the lengths of all ArgumentList items plus 3 per item (quotes and a space) is greater than 30000; the too-long test uses a test command of 40,000 characters. (4) fake-delegate.ps1 records the raw command line, [Environment]::CommandLine, to fake-delegate-args.txt (not its bound parameter values), and the recorded-arguments test asserts on that raw text: the -Command value appears as one quoted token that starts with [Console]::OutputEncoding and ends with exit $LASTEXITCODE, and -Feature, -Repo, -Worktree and -TimeoutSec carry the expected values. (5) In the mapping, check for an error starting 'sandbox: no free slot' (slot-busy) before the generic ok:false -> sandbox-error rule.

tasks.title: build stage and skill docs for sandboxed verify and phase tests
tasks.test: pwsh -NoProfile -c '$b = Get-Content -Raw skills/feature/stages/build.md; $f = Get-Content -Raw skills/feature/SKILL.md; $d = Get-Content -Raw skills/delegate/SKILL.md; $need = @(@($b, "-Feature <name>"), @($b, "-TimeoutSec 3600"), @($b, "verify -OnHost"), @($b, "slot-busy"), @($b, "environment-missing"), @($b, "host run: phase"), @($f, "verify"), @($d, "-Worktree"), @($d, "XAGENT_DELEGATE_SCRIPT")); $bad = @($need | Where-Object { -not $_[0].Contains($_[1]) } | ForEach-Object { $_[1] }); if ($b.Contains("lists at least one Python project")) { $bad += "old Python-only phase rule still in build.md" }; if ($bad.Count) { "missing: " + ($bad -join ", "); exit 1 }; "ok"'
tasks.brief: Update the three docs as the design's Files rows for them state, in the existing plain-language style of each file. stages/build.md: the verify step (cap rule first; the environment-input rule; read test.setup.status before test.passed with the environment-missing, slot-busy and sandbox-error handling; the host fallback: read tail, ask the user quoting the failing lines when it looks like a sandbox limit, and on a yes run verify -OnHost -Quote with the user's words); phase end and 'merge main' always run the phase test through delegate.ps1 -SandboxRun -Repo <repo> -Base feature/<name> -Feature <name> -Command <test> -TimeoutSec 3600, with the environment-missing flow, the one slot retry, and the host fallback logged by the lead as 'host run: phase <n>, approved: <words>' before running in <repo>. Remove the old 'only when the report lists Python projects' condition. feature/SKILL.md: the cap rule counts sandboxed verify and phase-test runs. delegate/SKILL.md: the -SandboxRun row names -Worktree, -Feature and the tail field; XAGENT_DELEGATE_SCRIPT is a test-only override read by feature.ps1; the Environments paragraph says the feature skill runs task and phase tests through -SandboxRun in every repo. Keep the feature tests' template and fixture checks passing. The acceptance command checks that key strings are present (see the test); the lead reads the text against the design. The phrase 'lists at least one Python project' from today's phase-end step must be gone.
